original_question:
For the hyperbolic or non-elliptic cubic NLS

 i partial_t v + (Delta_perp - partial_z^2)v + |v|^2 v = 0

in dimensions 2 and 3, can one prove that every H^1 solution is global, despite the lack of the standard elliptic structure of the usual focusing cubic NLS?
target_in_paper: Section 4.2, Open Problem 6: prove that the solutions to equation (69), the normal-GVD hyperbolic/non-elliptic cubic NLS, are global in dimensions 2 and 3. ([david-lannes.perso.math.cnrs.fr](https://david-lannes.perso.math.cnrs.fr/wp-content/uploads/2019/01/dumaslannesszeftel.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the exact PDE from the paper (equation (69)), its usual names (hyperbolic cubic NLS / non-elliptic cubic NLS), the relevant dimensions d=2,3, and the paper’s actual H^1 global-existence target. ([david-lannes.perso.math.cnrs.fr](https://david-lannes.perso.math.cnrs.fr/wp-content/uploads/2019/01/dumaslannesszeftel.pdf))
missing_details: The ambient domain should be stated explicitly: x=(X_perp,z) lies in R^d = R^(d-1) x R, with Delta_perp = partial_x^2 in d=2 and Delta_perp = partial_x^2 + partial_y^2 in d=3. ([david-lannes.perso.math.cnrs.fr](https://david-lannes.perso.math.cnrs.fr/wp-content/uploads/2019/01/dumaslannesszeftel.pdf))

The quantifier should be attached to initial data: for every complex-valued v_0 in H^1(R^d), does the corresponding maximal H^1 solution with v(0)=v_0 exist for all forward times? This is the paper-faithful meaning of solutions are global in the paragraph immediately preceding Open Problem 6. ([david-lannes.perso.math.cnrs.fr](https://david-lannes.perso.math.cnrs.fr/wp-content/uploads/2019/01/dumaslannesszeftel.pdf))

To match the paper exactly, the equation should be identified as the normal-GVD specialization of the general family (3), namely P_2 = I, alpha_1 = -1, alpha_2 = 0, alpha_3 = 0, and f = 0. ([david-lannes.perso.math.cnrs.fr](https://david-lannes.perso.math.cnrs.fr/wp-content/uploads/2019/01/dumaslannesszeftel.pdf))

The draft does not say that the paper isolates this bare equation (69), not more general variants with damping, ionization, self-steepening, or off-axis dependence. ([david-lannes.perso.math.cnrs.fr](https://david-lannes.perso.math.cnrs.fr/wp-content/uploads/2019/01/dumaslannesszeftel.pdf))

The nearby pulse-splitting issue is a separate official problem (Open Problem 7), so it should not be merged into the global-existence question unless explicitly asked. ([david-lannes.perso.math.cnrs.fr](https://david-lannes.perso.math.cnrs.fr/wp-content/uploads/2019/01/dumaslannesszeftel.pdf))
refined_question:
Let d be 2 or 3, write x=(X_perp,z) in R^(d-1) x R, and let Delta_perp = partial_x^2 when d=2 and Delta_perp = partial_x^2 + partial_y^2 when d=3. For each complex-valued initial datum v_0 in H^1(R^d), consider the maximal H^1 solution v:[0,T_max) x R^d -> C of the normal-GVD (hyperbolic/non-elliptic) cubic NLS:

i partial_t v + (Delta_perp - partial_z^2)v + |v|^2 v = 0,
 v|_{t=0} = v_0.

Is it true that T_max = +infinity for every v_0 in H^1(R^d), i.e. that all H^1 solutions to equation (69) are global in dimensions 2 and 3? ([david-lannes.perso.math.cnrs.fr](https://david-lannes.perso.math.cnrs.fr/wp-content/uploads/2019/01/dumaslannesszeftel.pdf))
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, using the H^1 local well-posedness and blow-up alternative stated just before Open Problem 6, does equation (69) admit any finite-time blow-up solution with initial data v_0 in H^1(R^d) for d=2 or 3? ([david-lannes.perso.math.cnrs.fr](https://david-lannes.perso.math.cnrs.fr/wp-content/uploads/2019/01/dumaslannesszeftel.pdf))
justification: The draft clearly targets Section 4.2 rather than the earlier derivation/approximation results, because its PDE matches equation (69) exactly. The nearest official formulation is therefore Open Problem 6, not a broader question about modified NLS models in general. The surrounding Section 4.2 discussion supplies the stand-alone details needed to sharpen the draft: H^1 local well-posedness and blow-up alternative, conservation laws in the energy space, the mass-critical/supercritical scaling remarks, the fact that the virial analogue is too weak, the absence of standing waves in the energy space, and the neighboring but separate pulse-splitting problem. The refined version keeps only that official global-existence problem and makes explicit the domain, operator notation, initial-data class, and maximal-lifespan quantifier. ([david-lannes.perso.math.cnrs.fr](https://david-lannes.perso.math.cnrs.fr/wp-content/uploads/2019/01/dumaslannesszeftel.pdf))
